episodes.179432: Daytime heating contributed to scattered thunderstorms that developed in the afternoon and evening along a surface boundary.  Aided by dry air aloft, some of the storms reached severe limits.
episodes.179433: Daytime heating contributed to isolated thunderstorms in the afternoon and evening, some of which produced sub-severe wind and some wind damage.
episodes.179462: Isolated storms developed along a surface trough in a moderately unstable environment during the afternoon and evening hours. Significant mid level dry air and a near surface dry layer supported a strong wind threat. Most of the severe reports were wind damage.
episodes.179463: Isolated storms developed along a surface trough in a moderately unstable environment during the afternoon and evening hours. Significant mid level dry air and a near surface dry layer supported a strong wind threat. Most of the severe reports were wind damage.
episodes.179482: A blocking pattern allowed anomalous moisture to be drawn into northeast Montana causing numerous thunderstorms, with locally heavy rainfall and dime sized hail.
episodes.179540: A closed low pressure system moved slowly eastward across southern California during the evening of June 6 and morning of June 7. Showers and thunderstorms developed over Kern, Kings and Tulare Counties during this time frame as the low moved through the area. Some of the thunderstorms produced brief heavy rainfall resulting in roadway flooding near Bakersfield and Delano.
episodes.179546: An upper-level low off the coast of California helped funnel in subtropical moisture into the state resulting in the development of widespread showers and storms across central and eastern New Mexico June 5th and 6th. Reports of severe weather and flash flooding stretched from the Rio Grande Valley across portions of eastern NM on June 5th. These reports ranged from a landspout tornado near the Petroglyph National Monument and Nara Visa, NM to flash flooding. Another round of severe weather began in the afternoon of June 6th producing more widespread reports over the same area of the state. Reports ranged from burn scar flash flooding within the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and Santa Rosa, to large hail over parts of San Miguel County.
episodes.179568: Severe thunderstorms moving offshore produced severe wind gusts near Cape Canaveral and in Lake County and a tornado in South Patrick Shores.
episodes.179569: Strong thunderstorms produced strong to severe wind gusts along the Brevard County coastline.
episodes.179999: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front during peak heating during the afternoon across portions of the Prairie Coteau and James River Valley. A brief landspout tornado was reported in the Clark area between roughly 2:30 pm and 2:45 pm CDT.
episodes.180048: A round of afternoon convection developed over the northern mountains of NM. One cell produced a funnel cloud while strengthening over U.S. Highway 84 near Cebolla, NM. No damage or touchdown was reported.
episodes.180081: A very moist, easterly surface flow advected 50 to 60 degree dewpoints from the central plains into the Billings Forecast Area. In addition, atmospheric precipitable waters were well over 1.00. Steering winds were light resulting in slow-moving thunderstorms. Although some large hail occurred with a few thunderstorms, the main impact was heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.180386: During the afternoon and evening hours of the 7th, clusters of severe storms moved from the NW to the S through Eastern North Dakota. These storms produced large hail and wind damage across Eastern North Dakota.
episodes.180438: A dominant west coast sea breeze regime triggered scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon, with strong to pulse severe storms developing toward the Atlantic coast where boundaries merged. Steep low level lapse rates and high CAPE supported hail and strong wind gusts in stronger cells.
episodes.180815: Anomalous atmospheric moisture combined with slow moving thunderstorms caused copious amounts of rain and in some places flooding.
episodes.180990: Isolated to Scattered diurnally driven thunderstorms formed over Central GA in the afternoon and evening hours. Storms moved generally Eastward with a few becoming severe mostly just South of Macon. Gusty winds of up to 60mph brought down several trees in the area.
episodes.181180: Scattered thunderstorms occurred across the coastal waters, a few of which produced gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well as a couple of waterspouts.
episodes.181319: Numerous ordinary-type thunderstorms developed across the forecast area from the early afternoon into evening of the 7th. A storm in Atoka County produced a report of severe-criteria hail.
episodes.181430: Thunderstorms developed across southwest Idaho early Tuesday evening and produced |heavy rain and strong winds across portions of the Lower Treasure Valley, including the city of Boise. Social media, weather spotters, and emergency manager reports indicated flooding of many streets in downtown Boise and the North-End Boise area. Water overwhelmed  storm water drainages and flowed onto sidewalks and lawns. Water up to two feet deep left several vehicles stranded in the downtown area. The Connector, a major commuter route to downtown Boise was flooded, as were some apartments, and several buildings on the Boise State University campus. Rainfall rates over one inch an hour occurred with localized  rainfall totals up to 1.85 inches between 6 PM and 10 PM MDT. ||Blowing dust reducing visibility and high winds formed with a strong outflow boundary near the Nevada border around 5pm MDT. Wind damage was reported from Grandview, ID to downtown Meridian, ID.
episodes.181511: Several rounds of rain and thunderstorms affected much of Montana during the first half of June. Flash flooding occurred across portions of the region, especially across Fergus County as well as the Rocky Mountains. Fergus County was hit exceptionally hard as several days of occasional heavy rain exasperated area creeks and streams. Casino Creek, located south of Lewistown, was washed out in at least two locations with significant road repairs required. Cottonwood Creek to the west of Casino Creek completely washed out Cotton Creek Road in several areas. Across the Rocky Mountains, easterly flow compressed moisture along the Rocky Mountain Front Range resulting in heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. Several debris flows were reported. Portions of Glacier National Park were temporarily closed due to rock slides and debris flows. The Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest also reported several flooding impacts. Across Meagher and Broadwater Counties, heavy rain affected the Woods Creek and Deep Creek burn scar areas, resulting in flash flooding along Highway 12. Flash flooding also occurred just south of Great Falls along Wilson Butte Road from a rapidly developing thunderstorm that produced 1.37 inches of rain in less than an hour at a NWS employee's home along Wilson Butte Road. A brief tornado also occurred across rural Hill County and was greatly photographed, but no damage was reported.
episodes.181738: Multiple rounds of storms impacted northeast Iowa from the afternoon of June 6th into the evening hours. One storm produced severe 1 inch hail near Alpha (Fayette County).
episodes.181800: With a weak surface high pressure moving east into the Atlantic, a shortwave trough over the Gulf of Mexico advected over the Florida Peninsula early on Wednesday. This created an early start for convection as showers and storms that began to develop by the morning hours over the Atlantic Ocean.
episodes.181982: An upper low was located over southern California with west to southwest flow aloft over the Borderland.  A surface low was located along the Rio Grande Valley which brought southeast surface winds to the El Paso area and provided plenty of wind shear for severe storms to develop around the county.
episodes.182008: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 6th. The strongest storms produced hail up to quarter size, and damaging wind.
episodes.182011: Thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon of the 7th. The strongest storm produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.182148: Continued lee troughing ahead of a large shortwave trough across the southwestern U.S. and a leading shortwave trough helped develop afternoon thunderstorms. These thunderstorms were largely sub-severe but one thunderstorm produced severe winds in rural Culberson County.
episodes.182151: A weak disturbance within the sub-tropical jet stream and a stationary front across the Permian Basin aided in the development of numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced large hail, severe winds, and flash flooding across portions of the region.
episodes.182214: A low pressure trough and sea breeze circulation within an environment displaying favorable instability and shear led to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.182368: Lightning struck a shed setting it ablaze.
episodes.182389: Thunderstorms brought rain and gusty outflow winds to portions of northern Utah.
episodes.182811: The beginning of a very wet month began with flash flooding and a few severe weather reports in early June. There was a closed low pressure located over California bringing Pacific based moisture over southern Colorado.
episodes.183332: An area of of resistant aufeis in the main channel of the Sagavanirktok (Sag) River during spring breakup forced the Sag River flow toward Milepost 403 of the Dalton Highway. The high flow from snowmelt and a heavy rain on snow event in the Brooks Range on June 10th exacerbated the impacts to the Dalton Highway.

The main flow of the Sagavanirktok (Sag) River was diverted to the farthest west channel of the river due to aurfeis blocking the channel. The Sag River was pushed up against the Dalton Highway and began to erode the road near Milepost 403.5. On June 7th the road was closed at Milepost 403.5 due to the Sag River eroding the highway to the centerline with the threat of a total washout. This closure shut off the only road access to the oil fields on the North Slope of Alaska. The AK Department of Transportation immediately began hauling rock from a quarry 150 miles away in order to secure the road. The road reopened to one lane traffic on June 8th, although the threat of erosion continued for another week. Runoff from heavy rain and snowmelt in the headwaters of the Sag River reached Milepost 403.5 of the Dalton Highway on June 14th.

A National Weather Service Melbourne damage survey confirms that an EF-1 tornado impacted the South Patrick Shores community just south of Patrick Space Force Base. The tornado touched down initially in the Lighthouse Landing subdivision near the intersection of Lighthouse Landing St. and South Patrick Dr. The circulation continued on an east-northeast trajectory across the South Patrick Shores community before emerging into the Atlantic near Ocean Blvd. and SR A1A. The tornado was on the ground for approximately 1.0 mile, had a maximum width of approximately 300 yards, and peak winds estimated between 90-100 mph.||Brevard County Emergency Management conducted a damage assessment and noted numerous homes were affected with at least some damage, 25 homes with minor damage, and 10 with major damage. NWS meteorologists documented impacts on both the north and south sides of the tornadic circulation in an area bounded by SE 1st St. to the south and NE 2nd St. to the north. Numerous homes in this area experienced at least partial losses of their carports and awnings. Additionally, several homes lost portions of their roof, a few trees were uprooted, and between 6-10 power poles were snapped in this area.
